title: SDK: surface overload error codes + Retry-After; add jittered backoff example
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: Go SDK now exposes Redwood overload error codes and Retry-After for 429/503 responses; includes an example of exponential backoff with jitter and guidance to avoid retry storms.
commits: sdk: parse Retry-After and expose on *Error
sdk: map overload responses to typed OverloadError w/ RedwoodCode
docs/examples: add safe retry w/ jitter and cap; include context cancellation
tests: add coverage for Retry-After variants + OpenAI-style error payloads
body:
Summary: Improves Go SDK error handling for overload/load-shedding responses so customers get actionable signals instead of generic 5xx. Specifically: (1) surfaces Redwood overload reason codes (when present) on a typed error; (2) parses and exposes Retry-After across 429/503 responses; (3) adds an example showing exponential backoff with jitter (and a max cap) to reduce retry storms.

Context: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding is rolling out, and we expect to return consistent 429/503 responses with Redwood-specific error codes and Retry-After guidance. Today the Go SDK collapses most non-2xx responses into a generic error and drops headers, which leads some clients to implement tight retry loops. This PR aligns the SDK behavior with the new customer-facing semantics defined in the overload program and support guidance.

Behavior changes (non-breaking): - Introduces a typed error: type OverloadError struct { StatusCode int; RedwoodCode string; Message string; RetryAfter time.Duration; RequestID string } - For 429 and 503 responses, the SDK attempts to populate OverloadError when the response body matches either the Redwood schema or the OpenAI-compatible error envelope used by our compat endpoints. - Adds parsing for Retry-After per RFC 9110 (delta-seconds) and a best-effort parse for HTTP-date. If parsing fails, the raw header remains accessible via ResponseHeaders on the base error.

Public API: - Existing error return types are preserved; callers using errors.As(err, *sdk.OverloadError) can detect overload explicitly. - Adds helper: retry.ShouldRetry(err error) bool and retry.SuggestDelay(err error, attempt int) time.Duration, which prefers Retry-After when present and otherwise uses exp backoff with jitter.

Example added: examples/overload_retry/main.go demonstrates: - honoring Retry-After when provided; - exponential backoff with full jitter and a max delay cap; - retry budget (max attempts and overall deadline); - no retries for non-retryable 4xx; - correct handling for streaming vs non-streaming requests (we avoid auto-retry once a stream has started producing bytes).

Notes / edge cases: - If a request returns 503 with a non-overload internal error, we do not force it into OverloadError unless a Redwood overload code is present or the payload matches the overload schema. This is intended to preserve debuggability for true server errors. - We also plumb x-redwood-request-id into the error for support escalations.

Test plan: - Added unit tests covering Retry-After parsing (delta-seconds, http-date, invalid values). - Added tests for mapping both Redwood-native error bodies and OpenAI-compat error bodies into OverloadError. - Ran examples/overload_retry against staging by forcing 429s via low quota and 503s via overload test harness; verified delays and jitter.

Screenshots/log snippets (example run): attempt=1 status=503 code=RWD_OVERLOAD_QUEUE_FULL retry_after=2s delay=2s attempt=2 status=503 code=RWD_OVERLOAD_QUEUE_FULL retry_after= delay=1.6s attempt=3 status=200 success=true

Review notes / follow-ups: - This PR does not change default client retry behavior globally; it only adds typed errors + helpers + examples. We can discuss whether to add an opt-in retry policy on the Client in a separate PR once we have more canary data.

Linked: Linear ENG-4836 (SDK surfacing overload semantics), ENG-4823 (standardized overload payload/headers). Support context: SUP-3961 (Retry-After interpretation) and SUP-3974 (client retry loop without jitter).

---

Review conversation:

Monica Patel: Can we make sure the typed error doesn’t trigger for generic 503s? We shouldn’t hide internal server errors as “overload”.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Yep — mapping requires either (a) a recognized Redwood overload code OR (b) a body matching the overload schema (including code field). Generic 503s will stay as APIError with status/message and request id.

Brian Murphy: Please confirm we parse Retry-After correctly and don’t treat milliseconds as seconds.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Parsing is strictly delta-seconds per spec (integer seconds) or HTTP-date. Added tests to ensure “2000” is 2000 seconds (and we cap via SuggestDelay).

Rafael Mendes: Jitter strategy? We’ve seen retry synchronization amplify incidents.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Implemented full jitter (rand[0, base]) with cap and uses Retry-After when present. Example recommends adding a per-request retry budget + overall timeout.

Wei Chen: Can you add a short README snippet pointing folks to the example and recommending honoring Retry-After?

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added a short section under “Handling rate limits and overload” with link to examples/overload_retry.

Approvals: Monica Patel approved; Brian Murphy approved; Rafael Mendes approved; Wei Chen approved.

CI: gofmt/lint passed; unit tests passed; staticcheck passed; examples build passed.

Merged (squash) into main.
